b: Netflix is taking another stroll through Old New York’s ballrooms—and, if showrunner Emma Frost is to be believed, its bedrooms too. The streamer today unveiled first-look images from The Age of Innocence, an eight-episode limited series adapted from Edith Wharton’s 1920 novel. All episodes premiere on Netflix on February 18, 2027.

Ben Radcliffe stars as Newland Archer, the well-bred lawyer engaged to May Welland (Kristine Frøseth) who falls hard for her unconventional cousin, Countess Ellen Olenska (Camila Morrone). Margo Martindale plays Mrs. Manson Mingott, the formidable grandmother of May and Ellen, while Fiona Glascott, Belinda Bromilow, Emma Shipp, and John Light round out the cast. Frost, who also writes and executive produces, says the story “is about the choice between following your heart or staying with duty and convention.”

Wharton’s novel, which made her the first woman to win the Pulitzer Prize for fiction, is best known on screen through Martin Scorsese’s 1993 film, which captures the exquisite agony and pleasure of passion. Frost’s version sounds rather less theoretical: Drawing on alternate endings Wharton sketched out, the series reportedly includes more explicit scenes, and it gives May and Ellen as much weight as Newland.
